annotation.title_clean: מפמ"כ 395 - תחנת עבודה של רובוט תעשייתי: דרישות בטיחות
annotation.title_en: Standard 395 - Industrial Robot Work Station: Safety Requirements (Standards Institution of Israel)
annotation.authors_or_issuer: מכון התקנים הישראלי (Standards Institution of Israel)
annotation.summary_en: Israeli Standard 395 (November 1993) sets safety requirements for industrial robot work stations, based on the Australian standard AS 2939. It specifies fencing and guards, interlocks, presence-sensing devices, trapped-key systems, limit switches, and multi-station layouts to keep people out of the robot's restricted zone.
key_provisions_or_claims: Robot work stations must be protected by safety fencing, presence-sensing devices, or other approved means.
Fixed and interlocked guards must meet specified opening sizes and safety distances (Table 1, Figure 1).
Presence sensing must detect entry into the restricted zone and stop automatic operation, with fail-safe control.
Interlock switching methods and trapped-key systems prevent restart while a guard is open.
Multi-station and multi-robot cells need separate restricted zones and emergency stops; components are to be approved by an authorised laboratory.
